classification.difficultyReason: Introduce an angle variable, link two distinct bisectors with parallel co-interior angles and eliminate the remaining triangle angle to prove a triple-angle identity; nonnumerical multistep proof.

content.prompt: $ABCD$ is a rhombus. The bisector of $\angle ABD$ meets $AD$ at $K$. Prove that $\angle AKB=3\angle ABK$.

spec.description: Rhombus with diagonal BD and supplied red dashed angle bisector BK. No right-angle marker is inferred.
spec.mathematics: Rhombus with diagonal BD and supplied red dashed angle bisector BK. No right-angle marker is inferred.
spec.answerVisibility: Original givens only; no answer values added.

answer.worked: Let $\angle ABK=\angle KBD=\alpha$. A rhombus diagonal bisects its vertex angle, so $\angle DBC=\angle ABD=2\alpha$ and $\angle ABC=4\alpha$. Since $AD\parallel BC$, $\angle BAK=180^\circ-4\alpha$. In triangle ABK, $\angle AKB=180^\circ-(180^\circ-4\alpha)-\alpha=3\alpha=3\angle ABK$.
